blocks.text: 工作原理

要启用 Tool Retrieval，在请求中添加一个 tool_search 工具，并在你希望暂缓加载的工具上设置 defer_loading: true。模型仍然能看到每个延迟工具的 name 和 description，因此知道有哪些工具可用，但参数 schema 不会进入上下文。当模型需要某个工具时，它会按名称请求，API 加载完整 schema，模型再调用该函数，整个过程都在同一个请求内完成。

blocks.text: 客户端检索如何工作
如果你维护自己的工具注册表、嵌入索引或按用户权限过滤，可以用 "execution": "client" 声明 tool_search 并定义搜索参数。客户端检索每次搜索会多一次往返，因为查找由你的应用执行。工具无需预先声明，因此当用户连接某个集成时，你也可以在对话中途暴露新工具：

tools = [{
    "type": "tool_search",
    "execution": "client",
    "name": "search_tools",
    "description": "Search the internal tool registry for functions.",
    "parameters": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {"query": {"type": "string"}},
        "required": ["query"],
    },
}]

# When the model emits a function_call for "search_tools",
# return matching {"type": "function", ...} schemas in function_result:
followup = client.interactions.create(
    model="gemini-4-hydrogen",
    previous_interaction_id=interaction.id,
    tools=tools,
    input=[{
        "type": "function_result",
        "name": "search_tools",
        "call_id": step.id,
        "result": my_registry.search(**step.arguments),
    }],
)

blocks.text: When an agent connects to dozens or even hundreds of tools, sending every full parameter schema on every request adds up fast. It inflates input token counts, adds latency, and lowers tool-selection accuracy as the candidate list grows. Tool Retrieval lets your agent keep its full tool library on standby and load parameter schemas only when the current task needs them.

blocks.text: How it works

To turn on Tool Retrieval, add a tool_search tool to your request and set defer_loading: true on the tools you want to hold back. The model still sees the name and description of every deferred tool, so it knows what's available, but the parameter schemas stay out of context. When the model needs a tool, it asks for it by name, the API loads the full schema, and the model calls the function, all inside the same request.

blocks.text: There's no index to build or host. Gemini runs the search on the server, so the only changes to your code are the new tool and a flag on the tools you want to defer. You can keep your most-used tools loaded up front and defer the long tail.

blocks.text: Tool Retrieval also plays well with prefix caching. Deferred schemas stay out of the start of the prompt, and the schemas the model loads are added later in the conversation, so the cached prefix stays the same from turn to turn.

blocks.text: How client-side retrieval works

If you maintain your own tool registry, embedding index, or per-user permission filter, declare the tool_search with "execution": "client" and define your search parameters. Client-side retrieval adds one round trip per search, because your app runs the lookup. Tools do not need to be declared upfront, so you can also expose new tools mid-conversation when a user connects an integration:

How pricing and supported models work

inlines.text: How pricing and supported models work

blocks.text: Tool Retrieval has no separate charge. Input and output tokens are billed at the standard rates for the model you call. Turning on tool_search adds a small, fixed block of input tokens, and each schema the model loads is billed as input for the rest of the conversation, the same as a tool declared up front. You save tokens when the schemas you never load outweigh the ones you do, which is the usual case for large libraries. Measure it against your own traffic.
